title: Conditionally smooth reactive curl without removing steady compression
hypothesis: Low-pass filtering capture curl preserves useful steady traction while suppressing compression impulses that eject the pen.

prediction.rationale: A 0.10 fresh sustained-success gain would make preserving compression dynamics worth pursuing; D-054's constant preload removed feedback entirely and therefore does not settle bandwidth reduction.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study r075_curl_bandwidth --log-dir logs/pen_spin/r075_curl_bandwidth"'
code_changes: New study module lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/curl_bandwidth.py registered as --study r075_curl_bandwidth in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py; settings in the research_protocols block of config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml. Parent config/pen_spin/r046_block3_incumbent (hashes checked), no fitting, parameters unchanged. No activation gate on any audit.

Filter, frozen: a first-order low-pass on extra_curl alone, y_t = y_{t-1} + alpha (x_t - y_{t-1}), alpha = dt / (tau + dt) with tau = 100 ms and dt = 1/60 s (alpha = 0.142857), kept per environment and initialised to the first raw value at reset; applied by one audited source substitution that wraps the extra_curl expression. Stroke, centring, rotation correction, parameters and execution unchanged; no search over the constant.

Identity gate, offline, before any episode: the wrapped source with alpha = 1 (the wrapper returns the raw value exactly) reproduces the parent's actions bit for bit on D-050's archived parent observations. Source audit as R-065.

Arms on one frozen 200-case Stage-3 manifest (seed 4642; cases 0-9 unused, promotion 10-39, fresh 40-199; placement-disjoint from every committed pen-spin manifest): parent; zero_curl (the exact R-068 clamp, a control); filtered_curl. Each arm runs each panel in its own fresh process: six processes, 570 evaluated episodes, zero LLM calls.

Primary: filtered_curl minus parent fresh sustained success (160 pairs), 95% t interval; prediction at least +0.10; supported if the mean is at least +0.10 and the lower bound is above zero; refuted if the upper bound is below +0.10 or if the filtered arm has an established drop increase against the parent; otherwise inconclusive. Secondary: filtered_curl minus zero_curl on both panels (retention kept, spin restored?), zero_curl minus parent (replication), and the raw versus filtered mean curl on recorded in-play steps. Repair qualification: strict promotion against both controls on the 30 promotion cases, fresh lower bound above zero against both, no observed drop increase against either on either panel.

Reported per panel and arm: sustained success, paired success and drop differences with intervals and win/loss/tie, failure split (drops, off-centre, slow spin), in-play mean |spin|, drive and per-axis executed-action saturation over recorded in-play steps. bc_steps 0, no imitation, no LLM repair, held-out split untouched.

falsified_by: The fresh paired interval's upper bound is below +0.10, or the filtered controller has an established increase in drops; an interval spanning zero is inconclusive, not improvement.

controls.parent: the unchanged frozen R-046 learner, each panel in its own process
controls.zero_curl: the exact R-068 clamp, each panel in its own process (control; third independent replication against the parent)
controls.identity_gate: the wrapped source at alpha 1 reproduced the parent's actions bit for bit on all 23,484 archived D-050 observations
controls.filter_effect_on_level: the filter changed the mean curl level by less than 0.2% (raw 0.410 vs filtered 0.410 on fresh), so the arm differs from the parent in timing only

notes: Primary, predeclared (160 fresh pairs): filtered curl minus parent -0.0938 [-0.170, -0.018] (24/160 vs 39/160; 12 wins, 27 losses, 121 ties): the upper bound is below +0.10 and below zero; refuted, and the filtered controller is worse than the parent. Drops 29 vs 21 (+0.0500 [-0.013, +0.113]), off-centre 56 vs 43. Promotion: 4/30 vs 6/30 (-0.0667 [-0.203, +0.070]), drops 10 vs 1 (+0.3000 [+0.126, +0.474], an established increase).

Against the zero-curl clamp the filtered arm is far worse: fresh -0.1688 [-0.258, -0.079] (24 vs 51; drops 29 vs 6), promotion -0.3000 [-0.523, -0.077] (4 vs 13; drops 10 vs 0). No arm qualifies as a repair parent.

Mechanism: the 100 ms low-pass leaves the mean curl level unchanged (raw 0.410 vs filtered 0.410) and only delays it; the delayed arm spins faster than both others (5.59 rad/s fresh, 6.72 promotion) yet drops the pen most. So the parent's reactive curl is not harmful because it is fast; it is harmful because it compresses at all, and compressing late is worse than compressing promptly (the lag lets the pen slip before the grip tightens, then the tightening ejects it). Bandwidth is the wrong lever; removal (D-052) remains the right one.

Third independent replication of D-052 (secondary): zero-curl minus parent fresh +0.0750 [-0.022, +0.172] (51 vs 39; 37 wins, 25 losses), drops 6 vs 21 (-0.0938 [-0.139, -0.048]), off-centre 8 vs 43; promotion +0.2333 [-0.020, +0.487] (13 vs 6; drops 0 vs 1), strict rule missed again by 0.02. Pooled over the three fresh panels (480 pairs, not predeclared): 148 vs 101 successes (+0.098), drops 23 vs 68; per-panel fresh gains +0.150, +0.069, +0.075, all positive; promotion gains +0.200, 0.000, +0.233.
Saturation: drive above 0.99 on 90-99% of recorded in-play steps in every arm; executed-action saturation 4-7% of components.

Accounting: 570 Isaac episodes in six fresh processes, 0 LLM calls, about 6 min wall time. Deviations: none; protocol.seeds was emptied mechanically after approval because the committed manifest carries seed 4642. Final-test split untouched.

verdicts.reasoning: Predicted that a 100 ms low-pass on the reactive capture curl would beat the parent by at least +0.10 fresh sustained success; observed -0.094 [-0.170, -0.018] on 160 pairs (24 vs 39; 12 wins, 27 losses), upper bound below +0.10 and below zero, with more drops (29 vs 21 fresh; 10 vs 1 on promotion, an established increase): refuted twice over by the predeclared rules, and the filtered controller is worse than the parent. Against the zero-curl clamp it is far worse (-0.169 [-0.258, -0.079]; drops 29 vs 6). The filter left the mean curl level unchanged (0.410 vs 0.410) and only delayed it, so the lesson is about timing: compressing late is worse than compressing promptly, and both are worse than not compressing. Bandwidth is the wrong lever; removal is the right one. Secondary: the zero-curl clamp beat the parent on a third independent fresh panel (51 vs 39, +0.075 [-0.022, +0.172]; drops 6 vs 21) and on the promotion panel (13 vs 6, +0.233 [-0.020, +0.487], strict rule missed by 0.02); pooled over 480 fresh pairs it is +0.098 with drops 23 vs 68. Confidence 0.92: exact identity gate, 160 pairs, consistent direction on both panels.
verdicts.next_experiment: Close the curl question: remove, do not reshape or retime. The zero-curl clamp has now beaten the parent on three independent fresh panels (all positive, pooled +0.098 over 480 pairs, drops cut by two thirds) and on two of three promotion panels, missing the strict 30-case rule each time by 0.006-0.02; the advisor and I should decide at the next triage whether the pooled fresh evidence qualifies it as the repair parent for the deferred stroke-side ideas (R-064 timing feedback, R-070 synchronous unloading, R-076 waveform shaping), or whether a 90-case promotion panel is needed first.
